title: Pen-and-ink drawings sold for charity
summary: Leeman says he majored in art in high school, drew a pen-and-ink series at Nick's in 1950, and plans to sell prints for a sheriff's charity.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: I have a bit about my religious views that you might want to get into later on. And another thing, about my -- when I was in high school, I majored in art, pen and ink especially, and I did a whole series of pictures of pen and inks when I was with Bobby Hackett in 1950 at the Nick's in the Village, and there are only a very few copies of these originals that I have given -- there are 10 actually finished that I have given to people who are close acquaintances and very soon I'm gonna have some prints made, and I'm gonna try to sell them for only one thing, for one of my pet charities. You know, I'm so -- I think so much of that
Hector sheriff's department down in Texas, I would like to sell some of those drawings so that I can contribute to that fund, their charitable fund, along with some church contributions.
